text: he says, "remember the first time that you flew, how you'd never been so high, (but then, you'd never needed to be?)".
and as though in reply, she speaks and she says "reasons are no substitute for reason",
and in the rime of london's cold, black teary eye these two have their conversation, while above them, a thin wall of cool air stalls the possibility of electrical storms.
that storm will not happen now, though possibility, the thing itself, lives on:
it moves from the chance of a storm to a baby being born,
from the accident at the crossroads to the overheard finality of a last conversation between two lovers,
from the river to the road,
from the word to the ward,
it can never be quelled or stilled completely, possibility. you've sensed it yourself: possibility positively crackles with potential. it's just not in the nature of possibility to stop.
so that's what it does, it keeps going: that's its purpose.
knowing this to be the case, possibility is hanging in there full of captured energy with the pull and shove of gravity and chance working away at it, until…
an unbidden shift occurs, possibility seizes its moment, does its gravity/chance thing and suddenly we're all looking at the world anew.
in the meantime, memory pulses away in the background until we call on it to make sense of our changing perspective.
this is the parallax between now and then.
